title: Viral Video of a Security Incident

opening.text: Have you seen it? Forty seconds of a guard dragging a man across our lobby floor. Two million views since midnight, and the owners are asking me what we're going to say. Boardroom, now.

briefing: 08:10, Saturday. A guest's phone video shows a Tessmore contract guard pulling a man across the Harbourfront lobby by his collar at 01:30. It has two million views. The man is not named.

Veldane incident communications method: the full facts before any judgement (all the footage, the reports, the people); a short holding statement within the hour that shows care and says what you're doing, without blaming anyone or prejudging; reach out to the man directly and privately; stand the officer down from duty pending the investigation, without announcing an outcome; preserve everything; involve the police if a crime may have been committed; let communications lead the public words and LP lead the facts; publish what changes once the investigation is done. Your authority is 3,000,000.

context.text: It is the second time in a year a Harbourfront staff member has made the news for stepping in. The owners will ask about training.
A man was held in the back office during the chargeback case. The press may connect them.

learningObjectives: Facts first, then a holding statement within the hour
Care for the person, without prejudging
Stand down, investigate, then change and say so

actions.label: Pull every camera angle of 01:20 to 01:40
actions.finding: L-01 and L-02 show what the phone didn't: at 01:24 the man, very drunk, swings at the night agent across the desk and knocks a monitor over. The guard asks him three times to step away. At 01:29 the man shoves the guard; the guard takes him by the collar and pulls him across the floor to the doors, well past the point where he was no longer a danger, and pushes him outside. Exported and logged as KC-3301.

actions.label: Read the night's reports and talk to the night agent
actions.finding: Tariq's statement, written at 02:00: frightened, and grateful the guard came. He also says the guard 'kept going after he'd stopped fighting'. The guard's own report says 'guest escorted from premises' and nothing more.

lines.speaker: desk_agent
lines.text: He saved me from getting hit. And then he didn't stop. Both of those are true.

actions.label: Agree a holding statement with the GM
actions.finding: "We've seen the video of an incident in our lobby early this morning and we are concerned by it. We are reviewing all our footage and speaking to everyone involved, and the officer is not on duty while we do. We are trying to contact the guest to make sure he's all right. We will share what we find." No blame, no defence, no outcome.

lines.speaker: gm
lines.text: Short, true, and nothing we'll have to take back. Send it.

actions.label: Put out a statement that the guest was violent first
actions.finding: The statement says the guest attacked staff and the officer acted in self-defence. Within an hour someone posts the full forty seconds slowed down: the man is limp on the floor for the last twenty. The statement becomes the story.

schedules.description: The 'self-defence' statement is quoted in every follow-up story; the guest's lawyer uses it to show the hotel defended the indefensible.

actions.label: Have counsel demand the poster takes the video down
actions.finding: The poster publishes the lawyer's letter. 'Hotel tries to silence witness' is the next headline, and the video's views double.

schedules.description: The takedown demand becomes its own story, and the hotel's name is now linked to silencing witnesses.

actions.label: Have the officer stood down pending the investigation
actions.finding: Callum takes the officer off the Harbourfront contract while Tessmore and the hotel investigate together; he stays on pay, and Tessmore offers him welfare support. Callum asks for the full footage for Tessmore's own investigation; it goes through the release process.

lines.speaker: guard_lead
lines.text: He's a good lad who lost his head at half one in the morning. That doesn't make it right. We'll do this properly.

actions.label: Reach the man directly and privately
actions.finding: He is a guest in 1311, checked in under his own name. Gideon calls him: is he hurt, does he need a doctor, the hotel is looking into it, here is a direct contact. He has a bruised shoulder and a hangover, and is ashamed of the first half of the video. He asks that his name never be given out; it won't be.

actions.label: Tell DS Calloway and offer the footage
actions.finding: Both men's actions may be offences; it is for the police and the man to decide whether to pursue them. DS Calloway logs it and requests KC-3301 through the release process.

actions.label: Finish the investigation and publish what changes
actions.finding: Findings with Tessmore: the removal was justified at first and excessive after the man stopped resisting; the officer's report was inadequate; night cover had one officer for the whole lobby. Changes: refresher training for all contract and in-house officers in de-escalation and safe holds, body-worn cameras on night patrol, two officers on the lobby after midnight at weekends, reports reviewed by LP each morning. A short public update says so, without naming anyone.

questions.prompt: Put the first hour in order
questions.explanation: You can't say anything true until you've seen what the phone didn't show. A holding statement then buys time without committing to a version. The person in the video matters more than the story, and the officer's stand-down protects everyone while the facts are found.

options.label: See all the footage and the reports
Stand the officer down pending the investigation

questions.prompt: Which holding statement do you put out?

options.label: Concerned, reviewing everything, the officer off duty meanwhile, trying to reach the guest, will share what we find.
options.feedback: It shows care and action and makes no claim the facts could later contradict.

options.label: The guest assaulted staff and the officer acted in self-defence.
options.feedback: Partly true and fatally incomplete. The rest of the video makes it the story.

options.label: No comment until the investigation is finished.
options.feedback: Silence for days is filled by everyone else's version.

questions.prompt: What happens to the officer now?

options.label: Off duty on pay pending a joint investigation with Tessmore, with welfare support.
options.feedback: It protects guests, the officer and the investigation, and decides nothing in advance.

options.label: Announce he has been dismissed.
options.feedback: An outcome before the facts, and it isn't yours to announce: he works for Tessmore.

options.label: Keep him on: the guest started it.
options.feedback: Whatever started it, the video shows force beyond the need. He can't be on the floor during the investigation.

questions.prompt: Which changes address what the investigation found?

options.label: De-escalation and safe-hold refresher for every officer
Two officers on the lobby after midnight at weekends
Every use-of-force report reviewed by LP each morning
Ban guests from filming in the lobby
options.feedback: The video showed a real problem. Fix that, not the camera.

options.label: 01:24 guest aggressive at the desk; 01:29 removed by contract officer, force excessive after resistance ended (KC-3301); officer stood down; guest contacted privately; police informed; training, night cover and report review changed; public update issued.
options.feedback: Both halves of what happened, what was done and what changed.

options.label: Contract officer used excessive force on a guest.
options.feedback: True, but it leaves out what came before and what the hotel changed.

options.label: Drunk guest attacked staff and was removed.
options.feedback: The half of the story that excuses the other half.

checks.label: Facts first
checks.pass: You saw all the footage before anything was said.
checks.fail: You spoke before you'd seen the footage.

checks.label: Within the hour
checks.pass: A holding statement was out within the hour.
checks.fail: The hotel was silent while the video spread.

checks.label: No takedown threat
checks.fail: The hotel tried to silence the person who filmed it.

checks.label: Stand down
checks.pass: The officer was off duty while it was investigated.
checks.fail: The officer stayed on the floor.

checks.label: Care for the man
checks.pass: He heard from the hotel privately and early.
checks.fail: He learned what the hotel thought from the news.

checks.label: Police told
checks.pass: The police knew and had the route to the footage.
checks.fail: The police learned of it from the news.

checks.label: Hear the witnesses
checks.pass: The night agent's account is in the file.
checks.fail: The only witness on staff was never heard.

checks.label: Change and say so
checks.pass: The investigation led to changes the public heard about.

debrief.whatHappened: A video showed half of an incident. You saw all of it before saying anything, put out a short, caring holding statement within the hour, stood the officer down without prejudging him, reached the man privately, told the police, and finished with changes the public could see.
bestPractice: All the footage and reports before any judgement.
A holding statement within the hour: care, action, no blame, no outcome.
Reach the person directly and privately.
Stand the officer down on pay pending a fair investigation.
Never threaten the person who filmed it.
Communications lead the words, LP leads the facts.
debrief.why: The public judges the hotel on what it does in the first hours, not on the incident alone. Care and honesty early earn the patience the investigation needs.

lesson: Facts first, holding statement in the hour, care without prejudging, stand down, change and say so.
